_comment: Golden vector for the audio OUTPUT STAGE of both implementations, so the two
can be compared without listening to them. The plugin (src/spyService.ts, the
ramp loop) and the standalone app (native-app/Sources/LocalRadio.swift level()
plus AudioSink.write) run the same three stages with the same constants:
per-mode makeup from MODE_MAKEUP / AudioLeveling.modeMakeup, an optional
output AGC that is off by default in both, and the tanh soft limiter at
0.85 x 32767. Every value below was produced by running the real code, not by
modelling it: test/audioLeveling.test.ts checks the `plugin` arrays and
native-app/Tests/main.swift checks the `solo` arrays.
THE ONE DIFFERENCE the vector pins down: the volume control sits on opposite
sides of the limiter. The plugin limits AFTER applying volume, the app limits
BEFORE and the sink applies volume afterwards. At volume 1.0 the two are
therefore identical (the `vol1` case, which is the control). Below the knee
they are identical at any volume. Above it, at volume 0.41, the app compresses
peaks the plugin passes through linearly: -0.9 dB at 24000, which is where the
AM carrier AGC's look-ahead ceiling puts peaks, and -3.5 dB at full scale.
Which is right is a real question and not settled here. Limiting after the
volume makes the limiter's threshold move with the knob, so the character of
the sound depends on the volume setting and at a low setting the limiter is
effectively absent. If the plugin is changed to match the app, the `plugin`
arrays here change with it and that is the deliberate signal.
